storyboard.claim: Humans tear each other apart inside the sealed town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim and Barbie locked in a fight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the closing chunk on the town turning on itself.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the 'shadow of the dome' into people fighting under it.

storyboard.claim: Marty applies the Sherlock rule: eliminate the impossible.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Andy frowning in thought, weighing options.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from inside the town to the outside investigation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the deduction method; the figure is a stand-in thinker, weak on identity.

storyboard.claim: Human technology cannot produce the barrier, so it must be alien.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia pondering the impossibility.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the deduction to its conclusion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout carries the claim; the face is neutral, so the words do the work.

storyboard.claim: Big Jim blames a government experiment on Barbie; the narrator calls it a lie.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim talking to the town with a smirk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Switches from the outside to Big Jim inside the town.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the claim as the narrator's rejected lie.

storyboard.claim: Big Jim believes the dome is God's will blessing his rule.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim speaking with a self-satisfied smirk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues Big Jim's self-serving story.
storyboard.addedInformation: Smirk shows the manipulative certainty, not warmth.

storyboard.claim: Humans bend the incomprehensible to serve their own agendas.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim pointing with a sly smile, bending the mystery to his use.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why Jim's story is self-serving.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout states the general claim; the figure is Jim as the example.

storyboard.claim: We assign the incomprehensible a narrative that benefits us.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim with a self-centered smirk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the point about self-serving narratives.
storyboard.addedInformation: Staging keeps the focus on Jim's self-centred framing.

storyboard.claim: Big Jim makes himself the center of the universe.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim raising his arms, pleased with himself.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrows the previous point onto Jim alone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Celebrating gesture shows his self-regard.

storyboard.claim: The alien purple box is a distracting sci-fi trope.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia thinking, sceptical.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the critical debate about the alien element.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout names the critique; face is doubtful.

storyboard.claim: The book's real analysis covers fascism, environmental collapse and town psychology.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three buckets of the book's analytic topics.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists what the analysis should focus on instead of the aliens.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sorter shows three separate topics, not one story.

storyboard.claim: The alien answer feels like a cheat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Andy slumped in disappointment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Voices the critic's complaint about the ending.
storyboard.addedInformation: Slump shows disappointment with the reveal.

storyboard.claim: The alien element is vital because it represents cosmic indifference.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie pointing, arguing against the critic.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opposes the previous complaint.
storyboard.addedInformation: Angry confrontation marks the disagreement.

storyboard.claim: The dome is like a cruel child's glass jar over ants.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sealed dome drawn as a glass jar over the town.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the metaphor King uses.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dome icon is literal: a sealed glass enclosure.

storyboard.claim: The alien frame shows how pathetic Big Jim's power grab is.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim slumped and diminished.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the jar metaphor to Jim.
storyboard.addedInformation: Blank apathy and slump show him diminished, not triumphant.

storyboard.claim: Big Jim thinks he is a god in Chester's Mill.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim talking with a self-regarding smirk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues on Jim's self-image.
storyboard.addedInformation: Smirk marks the arrogance.

callout.text: an ant fighting over a crumb

storyboard.claim: Big Jim is just an ant fighting over a crumb in a glass jar.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two men fighting, the scale of the struggle small.
storyboard.onScreenText: an ant fighting over a crumb
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shrinks Jim to the jar's scale.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fighting pose carries the ant-scale conflict; second figure is the rival.

storyboard.claim: The cosmic view humbles the dictator by ignoring him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia reacting with surprise.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Responds to the ant metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: Surprised reads as realisation, not fear.

callout.text: The dome is a pressure cooker

storyboard.claim: The dome is a pressure cooker; the humans make the terrarium a slaughterhouse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Andy slumped under the pressure.
storyboard.onScreenText: The dome is a pressure cooker
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the jar metaphor into the human pressure cause.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout carries the pressure-cooker image; face is worried.

storyboard.claim: The critic pauses to look at the whole book.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia thinking, stepping back from the story.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from the ant metaphor to a critique of the book.
storyboard.addedInformation: Think pose signals reflection.

storyboard.claim: Does the narrative structure hold, or is the deck stacked?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Andy frowning, weighing the structure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the structural critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout names the critique precisely.

storyboard.claim: The stage set may be too perfectly rigged for disaster.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia frowning in doubt.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the structural question.
storyboard.addedInformation: Worried face shows doubt, a question not an accusation.

storyboard.claim: Chester's Mill just happens to host one of the biggest meth labs in the country.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Big Jim thinking, unsettled by the discovery.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First of three coincidences.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout names the coincidence.

storyboard.claim: Junior's undiagnosed brain tumor drives him to murder on the day the dome falls.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three steps: brain tumor, murder, dome falls.
storyboard.onScreenText: A brain tumor drives Junior to murder
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Second coincidence, as a cause chain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Flow makes the causal chain explicit.

storyboard.claim: The old police chief with a pacemaker dies instantly, leaving a vacuum.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave icon beside the sad figure, the death of the moral police chief.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Third coincidence, the death.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grave reads as death; rusty stands in for the medical world, weak identity match.

storyboard.claim: Is the coincidence brilliant narrative acceleration or a contrived experiment?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia thinking, weighing the question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the critique into a question.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout frames the first possible reading.

storyboard.claim: The town may feel like a contrived laboratory experiment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia frowning at the question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Second side of the question.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout states the alternative reading.

callout.text: a loaded deck in a casino

storyboard.claim: The story is a loaded casino deck: Duke's pacemaker decides the outcome.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie thinking, uneasy about the rigged game.
storyboard.onScreenText: a loaded deck in a casino
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the casino image for the stacking.
storyboard.addedInformation: Casino image is literal enough to read as rigged.

storyboard.claim: Without these coincidences the town would have no scapegoat; Barbie is framed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie slumped, the framed man.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists how the coincidences set up the frame.
storyboard.addedInformation: Slump shows the burden on Barbie.

storyboard.claim: Every domino is placed to guarantee the worst outcome.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Andy thinking through the chain of events.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the chain argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout names the domino image.

callout.text: Not every town is this one

storyboard.claim: Chester's Mill is not meant to be Every Town USA.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia thinking.
storyboard.onScreenText: Not every town is this one
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the generic-town reading.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the narrator rejecting Every Town.

storyboard.claim: The town is a narrative pressure chamber built to yield human combustion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Andy thinking about the engineered setting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the chamber image.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout states the engineered-setting claim.

storyboard.claim: You have to accept the lab-experiment premise to enjoy the results.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia pointing, making a point to the viewer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concludes the coincidence argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Point gesture addresses the viewer.

callout.text: buy the ticket, take the ride

storyboard.claim: You buy the ticket and take the ride: the unsettling experience of the book.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia, afraid, reflecting on the ride.
storyboard.onScreenText: buy the ticket, take the ride
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts to the book's overall experience.
storyboard.addedInformation: Afraid face reads as the unsettling tone.

storyboard.claim: The book packs tyrants, scapegoats, the complicit and cosmic horror into one town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia, thinking, reviewing the list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises the book's roster of types.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout states the single-town claim.

storyboard.claim: We build walls and lock our doors seeking security.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door icon, locked, beside the worried figure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the closing thesis about security.
storyboard.addedInformation: Door reads as an entry barred shut.

storyboard.claim: The dome was a terrarium designed to trap the poison inside.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The dome drawn as a sealed enclosure over the town.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reveals the dome's purpose.
storyboard.addedInformation: Dome icon is literal: sealed inside, not keeping things out.

storyboard.claim: The rot is forced to consume itself inside the sealed town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Andy slumped, the town's decay.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the sentence from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Slump shows the decay, not a literal fire.

callout.text: We are all under the dome

storyboard.claim: Every one of us lives in a closed system: we are all under the dome.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The dome icon over the sad, reflective figure.
storyboard.onScreenText: We are all under the dome
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closing line of the chunk.
storyboard.addedInformation: Dome icon makes the closing metaphor literal.
